correctness.rationale: Exact Picard intersection pairings for all 22 negative curves are verified in verify_picard.py. Bezout and adjunction exhaust all negative curves; the Schur complement establishes the negative-definite support criterion. The Bauer–Funke–Neumann correspondence identifies all chamber supports. Three structurally distinct exhaustive algorithms, one by individual supports, one by whole Frobenius orbit unions, and one by independent star/triangle support families checking all 720 permutations, agree on every one of the eleven S6 cycle types, the full size refinements, and the sharp 8-versus-8 difference. Norm/averaging with an ample ground-field divisor realizes every stable negative support over Fq. Closed-point counts on a finite-field conic certify the exact q≥5 and q=3 realization bounds. No unproved infinite generalization is claimed.

value.rationale: The two numbers count actual Fq-realizable negative-support patterns of big divisors, a natural arithmetic refinement of a published geometric chamber invariant. They reconstruct all eleven Frobenius cycle types, and show a sharp one-count obstruction (4,2 versus 5,1) resolved by the uniquely distinguished conic root. This is a complete classification of a natural invariant rather than a cosmetic extra decimal or arbitrary sample. It makes no unsupported claims about moduli or chamber volumes.
